title: [internal] TLS HTTP2 startup peer-close logs wrapped socket option errors
body:
**Requesting repo:** duskmoon-dev/duskmoon-bundler on branch `main`

We are migrating local Phoenix/SSE fixtures from Bandit to Gaoxy. Normal clients can finish TLS ALPN negotiation and disconnect before sending an HTTP/2 request. Gaoxy 0.12.2 currently records some of these ordinary startup disconnects as abnormal connection-process failures.

**Severity:** nice-to-have

**Environment:** Elixir 1.18.5, OTP 28.5.0.7, Linux; `gaoxy_http` / `gaoxy` 0.12.2, `hell` 0.1.2. The Phoenix/SSE HTTP/2 feature suite passed all 37 cases; no request-delivery failure was observed. This issue concerns startup error classification and noisy logs.

**Minimal reproduction:** in a Mix project using `gaoxy_http == 0.12.2` and the explicit `websock_adapter` alias to `gaoxy_websock_adapter == 0.12.2`, create a test certificate:

```sh
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -days 1 -subj /CN=localhost -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem
```

Save this as `probe.exs` and run `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start probe.exs`. It performs 20 serial TLS connections, verifies negotiated ALPN `h2`, then closes each without sending a request. The code was run against the requesting repository's compiled dependency graph with its existing test certificate.

```elixir
ExUnit.start(autorun: false)
{:ok, _} = Application.ensure_all_started(:gaoxy_http)

defmodule GaoxyStartupCloseProbe do
  @behaviour Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts
  def call(conn, _opts), do: Plug.Conn.send_resp(conn, 200, "ok")
end

{:ok, server} =
  Gaoxy.HTTP.start_link(
    plug: {GaoxyStartupCloseProbe, []},
    ip: {127, 0, 0, 1},
    port: 0,
    transport: :tls,
    tls: %{
      certfile: Path.expand("cert.pem"),
      keyfile: Path.expand("key.pem")
    }
  )

%{local: {:ok, {_ip, port}}} = Gaoxy.info(server, :http)

log =
  ExUnit.CaptureLog.capture_log(fn ->
    results =
      1..20
      |> Task.async_stream(
        fn _ ->
          {:ok, socket} =
            :ssl.connect(~c"127.0.0.1", port,
              verify: :verify_none,
              active: false,
              alpn_advertised_protocols: ["h2"]
            )

          {:ok, "h2"} = :ssl.negotiated_protocol(socket)
          :ssl.close(socket)
        end,
        max_concurrency: 1,
        timeout: 5_000
      )
      |> Enum.to_list()

    true = Enum.all?(results, &match?({:ok, :ok}, &1))
    Process.sleep(100)
  end)

IO.puts("20 serial ALPN h2 connections closed before a request")
log
|> String.split("\n")
|> Enum.filter(&String.starts_with?(&1, "** (stop)"))
|> Enum.frequencies()
|> IO.inspect(label: "termination reasons")
Supervisor.stop(server)
```

**Actual:** the independent 20-connection run completed successfully at the client and captured 9 occurrences of:

```text
GenServer ... terminating
** (stop) {:options, {:socket_options, [buffer: 16384, recbuf: 16384], :einval}}
Process Label: {:hell, :connection, {Gaoxy.HTTP.Connection, ...}}
Last message: {:continue, :handle_connection}
```

The same error appeared once during the passing TLS browser suite.

**Expected:** classify a peer that closes during HTTP/2 initialization as an orderly connection closure, release its resources, and avoid an abnormal termination log. Keep real invalid-option failures visible.

**Source pointers:** `Gaoxy.HTTP.HTTP2.Connection.start/2` sets the 16 KiB receive/buffer options and propagates the wrapped OTP SSL error. `Gaoxy.HTTP.Connection.start_http2/2` already handles bare `:closed`, `:einval`, and `:enotconn` from earlier metadata checks, but the wrapped `{:options, {:socket_options, ..., :einval}}` from the later H2 initialization bypasses that handling. OTP SSL wraps an underlying inet setopts error in this shape. The timing is consistent with a peer-close race between TLS metadata collection and the H2 socket option update.

The requesting repository keeps its TLS assertions and logging intact; no local transport patch or blanket log suppression is being applied.
